events.title: Accusation Against Judah
events.description: Isaiah begins his book with a strong accusation from God against Judah and Jerusalem. Heaven and earth are called as witnesses: I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against me. The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's feeding trough, but Israel does not know my people. The people's sacrifices and festivals have become a burden to God because they combine outward worship with inner injustice. God calls them to wash themselves clean, stop doing evil, and learn to do good.

events.title: Isaiah's Call and Vision of Holiness
events.description: In the year that King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord sitting on a high and exalted throne, and the train of his robe filled the temple. Seraphim stood above him and called to one another: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts! The whole earth is full of his glory! Isaiah cried out woe to himself because he was a man with unclean lips. A seraph flew to him with a burning coal from the altar and touched his mouth and said that his guilt was taken away. When God asks whom he should send, Isaiah answers: Here I am, send me! He is given the task of preaching to a people who will hear without understanding.

events.title: The Sign of Immanuel to Ahaz
events.description: During the Syro-Ephraimite war, when Aram and the Northern Kingdom threatened Judah, God sent Isaiah to King Ahaz with a message to be calm and not fear. Isaiah asked the king to request a sign from the Lord, but Ahaz refused under the guise of piety. Then Isaiah said: The Lord himself will give you a sign. See, the young woman shall conceive and bear a son, and she shall name him Immanuel, which means God with us. Before the boy knows how to reject evil and choose good, the two kings that Ahaz fears will be gone.

events.title: A Child Is Born to Us
events.description: Isaiah proclaims that the people walking in darkness will see a great light. Over those living in the land of the shadow of death, the light will shine. A child is born to us, a son is given to us. The government will rest on his shoulders, and he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. His government and peace will have no end, sitting on David's throne and ruling over his kingdom. This prophecy is one of the most central messianic texts in the Old Testament.

events.title: The Shoot from the Stump of Jesse
events.description: Isaiah prophesies that a shoot shall spring from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots shall bear fruit. The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord. He will not judge by what his eyes see, but will judge the poor with righteousness. The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, the leopard shall lie down with the kid, and a little child shall lead them. No one shall do harm on all God's holy mountain, for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea bed.

events.title: Oracle against Babylon
events.description: Isaiah pronounces a burden against Babylon. The Lord musters an army for war from a distant land, from the ends of heaven. The day of the Lord is near; it comes as destruction from the Almighty. Babylon, the glory of kingdoms and the pride of the Chaldeans, will be like Sodom and Gomorrah. No one shall live there anymore; no Arab shall pitch a tent there, and no shepherd shall let his flocks rest there. Desert animals shall lie down there, and owls shall dwell in its magnificent palaces.

events.title: The Fall of the King of Babylon
events.description: In a taunt song against the king of Babylon, Isaiah describes his pride and downfall. The king says in his heart that he will ascend to heaven and exalt his throne above God's stars. He will rise above the heights of the clouds and make himself like the Most High. But he shall be cast down to Sheol, to the deepest part of the grave. Those who see him will stare at him and say: Is this the man who made the earth tremble and shook kingdoms? This text has traditionally also been interpreted as a description of Satan's fall.

events.title: Isaiah Goes Naked as a Sign
events.description: In the year that the Assyrian commander came to Ashdod and besieged and captured it, the Lord spoke through Isaiah. God commanded him to remove his sackcloth and sandals and go naked and barefoot. Isaiah did this for three years as a sign and warning against Egypt and Cush. Just as Isaiah has gone naked and barefoot, so will the king of Assyria lead away Egyptian captives and Cushite exiles, young and old, naked and barefoot. Those who trusted in Cush and Egypt will be put to shame.

events.title: The Lord's Feast on the Mountain
events.description: Isaiah prophesies about a future day when the Lord, the God of hosts, will hold a feast for all peoples on this mountain. It will be a feast with rich food and aged wine. On this mountain he will destroy the veil that covers all peoples and the shroud that enfolds all nations. He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord God will wipe away tears from all faces and remove the disgrace of his people from the whole earth.

events.title: The Precious Cornerstone
events.description: Amidst the woe cries over the drunkards of Ephraim and the leaders of Jerusalem, Isaiah proclaims that the Lord is laying a foundation stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation. The one who believes will not be put to shame. The Lord will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line. Hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and water will wash away the hiding place. This prophecy is referred back to in the New Testament as a prophecy about Christ.

events.title: The Way of the Redeemed
events.description: Isaiah concludes the oracles of woe with a glorious vision of future restoration. The desert shall bloom like a rose and rejoice with joy. The blind shall see, the deaf hear, the lame leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute sing for joy. There shall be a road there, a holy way. No unclean person shall travel on it; no lion shall be found there. But the redeemed of the Lord shall return and come to Zion with singing, eternal joy upon their heads. Joy and gladness will overtake them; sorrow and sighing will flee away.

events.title: Sennacherib's Siege of Jerusalem
events.description:
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah's reign, the king of Assyria, Sennacherib, marched up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.  
He sent his supreme commander, the Rabshakeh, to Jerusalem with a large army to demand surrender.  
The Rabshakeh mocked Judah and the Lord in front of the people on the wall.  
Hezekiah sent messengers to the prophet Isaiah, who replied that God would send a spirit upon the Assyrians so that the king would return home.  
Hezekiah prayed in the temple, and Isaiah prophesied Sennacherib's downfall.  
That same night, the angel of the Lord struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib returned to Nineveh, where he was later killed by his own sons.

events.title: Hezekiah's Illness and Healing
events.description: King Hezekiah becomes terminally ill, and the prophet Isaiah comes to him and says that he will die and not recover. Hezekiah turns his face to the wall and prays to the Lord with weeping, reminding God of his faithfulness. Before Isaiah has left the middle courtyard, the word of the Lord comes to him: Go back and tell Hezekiah that God has heard his prayer and seen his tears. He will be given fifteen years added to his life. As a sign, God causes the shadow to move ten steps backward on Ahaz's sundial. Hezekiah writes a song of praise after his healing.

events.title: Hezekiah Shows the Treasures to the Envoys of Babylon
events.description: King Merodak-Baladan of Babylon sends a letter and gifts to Hezekiah because he has heard about his illness and recovery. Hezekiah receives the messengers with joy and shows them all his treasure: the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, and his entire armory. There was nothing in his house or kingdom that Hezekiah did not show them. The prophet Isaiah comes to the king and asks what these men have seen. When Hezekiah tells him that he showed them everything, Isaiah prophesies that all that is in his house will be carried off to Babylon, and some of his descendants will become court officials in the palace of the king of Babylon.

events.title: Comfort, comfort my people
events.description: With a dramatic shift the second main part of Isaiah opens with God's word: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God. Speak warmly to Jerusalem and cry out to her that her struggle is ended, that her guilt is paid, that she has received double from the Lord’s hand for all her sins. A voice cries in the wilderness: Clear the way of the Lord, make a straight highway for our God! All flesh is like grass and all its glory like the flower of the field, but the word of our God stands forever. Isaiah proclaims that the Lord comes with power, but also as a shepherd who carries the lambs on his arm.

events.title: The Suffering Servant of the Lord - First Song
events.description: God presents his servant whom he has chosen, his beloved in whom his soul delights. He has put his Spirit upon him, and he will bring justice to the nations. He will not cry out or raise his voice, nor make his voice heard in the street. A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not quench. Faithfully he will bring forth justice. He will not fail or be discouraged until he has established justice on earth, and the coastlands wait for his teaching.

events.title: Second Servant Song
events.description: The Lord's servant speaks himself and says that the Lord called him from the womb and named him from his mother's womb. He made his mouth like a sharp sword and hid him in the shadow of his hand. God says to the servant: You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified. The servant answers that he has labored in vain, but his cause is with the Lord. It is too little for him merely to raise up the tribes of Jacob; God will also make him a light for the nations, so that his salvation may reach to the ends of the earth.

events.title: Third Servant Song
events.description: The Lord's servant testifies that the Lord God has given him a disciple's tongue, so that he may strengthen the weary with a word. Every morning God awakens his ear so that he may hear like a disciple. The servant was not rebellious and did not turn away. He gave his back to those who struck him, and his cheeks to those who pulled out his beard. He did not hide his face from shame and spitting. Because the Lord God helps him, he is not put to shame. He knows that the one who pleads his cause is near.

events.title: The Suffering Servant
events.description: The fourth and most well-known Servant Song portrays the Lord's servant as despised, rejected, and full of suffering. He bore our sicknesses and took upon himself our pains, yet we regarded him as struck down by God. He was wounded for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we have received healing. We all wandered like sheep, but the Lord laid on him all our guilt. He was mistreated, yet he did not open his mouth, like a lamb led to slaughter. He was taken away from the land of the living and given a grave among the wicked, though with a rich man in his death. This text is the Old Testament's clearest prophecy concerning Christ's suffering and substitutionary death.

events.title: Come, all you who are thirsty
events.description: Isaiah ends the Book of Consolation with a magnificent invitation from God: Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters! You who have no money, come, buy and eat! Buy wine and milk without money and without cost. Why spend money on what is not bread, and your wages on what does not satisfy? Seek the Lord while he may be found; call on him while he is near. Let the wicked forsake their way, and the unrighteous their thoughts; let them turn to the Lord, that he may have mercy on them. For as the rain and snow come down from heaven and do not return there but water the earth, making it bring forth seed and bread, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty.

events.title: The Lord's Spirit is upon me
events.description: Isaiah proclaims the anointed one's mission: The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and freedom to those who are bound. He has sent me to proclaim a year of favor from the Lord and a day of vengeance from our God, to comfort all who mourn. Jesus read this text aloud in the synagogue at Nazareth and said it was fulfilled in their hearing.

events.title: New heaven and new earth
events.description: Isaiah ends his book with God's promise of a completely new creation: "See, I create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered or come to mind." Rejoice and be glad forever in what I am creating! Infants will no longer die after only a few days, and no old man will die before his time is complete. The wolf and the lamb will graze together; the lion will eat straw like the ox, and the serpent will have dust for food. No one will do evil or harm on all my holy mountain," says the Lord. This vision points all the way to John's Revelation and the final restoration of all things.
